title: Support reading status code and response headers, even on failure

labels.name: needs implementer interest
labels.description: Moving the issue forward requires implementers to express interest

body:
### What problem are you trying to solve?

Allow reading the http status code and http response headers of the connect request for websocket both when it succeeds and when it fails from javascript API.

This is needed (together with #16) to bridge the gap between native runtimes access to websockets and web context runtime. 

Namely it is very useful to allow:
- proxies (e.g. L7 proxies s.a. AFD) can communicate failures to the client including things s.a. throttling which *might* require the client to detect these and adjust retries
  - This is especially problematic, as if we want to solve this via separate standard non-wss http request to get the state, we're now creating new request to be processed and possibly throttled, not great for cases where we already throttle.
- webservers can handle the connect attempts same as any other REST requests, i.e. communicate some failure states in status code, details in response headers (e.g. auth challenges)
- WSS / LongPoll can be handled in more similar way both at client and at server. And in more similar way between native SDKs and non-native SDKs.


### What solutions exist today?

None. You need to accept the WSS connection and send the error as application message which proxies mostly do not support it (as it means doing app-level and not protocol level stuff):

On webtransport side of things, it is now (https://github.com/w3c/webtransport/pull/713) possible to read the response headers and status code *if* the connect succeeds, but that doesn't solve most of the request. The ask to support reading these for failure is ongoing in: https://github.com/w3c/webtransport/issues/777

On server side, all runtimes (Go, .NET, ...) support this. 

### How would you solve it?

For API see how Webtransport, for security impact of happy path (successful connect) see https://github.com/w3c/webtransport/pull/713 and related. For discussion about security impact of the failure case see https://github.com/w3c/webtransport/issues/777 . 

Opt-in from server via `Access-Control-Expose-Headers` or `Access-Control-Expose-Status` would be perfectly acceptible.

### Anything else?

We're a huge WSS service and significant engineering resources are poured periodically into working around the lack of this and #16 . 

This one, specifically, costs not just engineering time but, due to inability of generic L7 proxies to communicate throttling state in way the client could communicate without additional requests, also significant compute footprint.

With the advent of LLM agents and thus resurgence of wss this issue is more pressing than ever. 

---

We're in contact with MSFT's edge team to help with this.
